evidence_requirement: Per-store table: store, key shape, repo source file:line, deployed copy file:line. A store armed in the repo but absent from the live tree is still live for anyone who deploys - it must be listed, not dismissed.
question_or_target: Audit and fix every piece of harness state that must be SESSION-keyed rather than PROJECT-keyed - goal injection, ledger replay, claims, caches - because a project-keyed key bleeds one session's goal into a concurrent sibling. Exact question: which state stores are currently project-keyed, checked in the REPO source and not only in the deployed copy?
reviewer_requirement: independent-claude-reviewer repeats the audit against the repo source specifically
tests_required: bleed test: two concurrent fixture sessions in the same project must not read each other's goal. Repo-versus-live control asserting the audit read BOTH.
title: Session-scoped state keying audit against goal bleed

evidence_requirement: Both-states CI evidence: the gate red on a deliberately invalid receipt and green on a valid one, with the run ids and the failing step name for the red run.
question_or_target: Ship the receipt validator as a command and wire it into the existing command-center CI gate so an invalid or missing receipt turns the gate red. Exact question: with a deliberately invalid receipt committed, does the gate actually fail, or does it pass because the validator is invoked in a mode where the check is a no-op?
reviewer_requirement: independent-claude-reviewer confirms the red run failed at the validator step and not elsewhere
tests_required: both-states gate test; a no-op-mode test asserting the validator cannot be invoked in a mode where it validates nothing.
title: Receipt validator command wired into the command-center CI gate

evidence_requirement: Before: the defaults-block-deleted mutation exits 0. After: the same mutation exits nonzero. Both exit codes recorded verbatim from the same command line.
question_or_target: Arm tools/command-center/validate.py field completeness: require_complete defaults to False and CI invokes the tool bare, so deleting the ENTIRE defaults block exits 0 and passes the gate. Exact target: after this unit, that same deletion must turn CI red.
reviewer_requirement: independent-claude-reviewer reproduces both the before and after exit codes
tests_required: the defaults-deletion mutation is the test; it must fail the gate. A second control mutation (delete one field only) must also fail.
title: Arm the disarmed work-unit field-completeness check in CI

evidence_requirement: Per-file digest table with three columns - working-tree hash, blob hash, recorded provenance hash - across all fourteen manifest entries, taken on a Windows checkout.
question_or_target: Fix the command-center provenance check so it hashes the COMMITTED blob rather than working-tree bytes, making it runnable on a Windows checkout where core.autocrlf rewrites line endings. Exact question: after the fix, do the Windows and Linux runs produce the same digest for all fourteen manifest entries?
reviewer_requirement: independent-claude-reviewer re-derives two digests by a different command than the implementation uses
tests_required: platform-parity test asserting the blob route yields identical digests on a CRLF and an LF checkout; a control asserting the working-tree route DIFFERS, proving the fix changed something.
title: Make the provenance hash read the committed blob, not the working tree

evidence_requirement: A time-series of observed concurrent units per substrate across a 40-unit mixed dry run; the local-serialized series must be flat at one.
question_or_target: Implement the dispatcher that reads the catalog and routes each unit to its declared execution_substrate, with local-serialized meaning strictly one at a time. Exact question: with a catalog containing units of all four substrates, does the observed simultaneous count for local-serialized ever exceed one?
reviewer_requirement: independent-claude-reviewer inspects the time-series, not the summary
tests_required: substrate-isolation test per substrate; a mutation removing the serial lock must show a concurrent count above one and turn the test red.
title: Work-unit dispatcher honoring the declared execution substrate

evidence_requirement: Decision table: failure class, configured policy, observed attempt count. Any class whose observed count differs from its policy is a defect.
question_or_target: Implement the retry engine so the retry decision is a pure function of the typed failure class, not of the raw error text. Exact target: a schema-invalid failure must be retried ZERO times, a provider transient up to its cap, and a second failure on the same fingerprint must trigger the two-strikes pivot rather than a third attempt.
retry_policy: max 2 attempts to implement; the engine must not be able to retry its own failure indefinitely
tests_required: one test per failure class; a same-fingerprint repeat test asserting the pivot fires at strike two, not strike three.
title: Retry-policy engine driven by typed failure classification

evidence_requirement: A control-plane census before and after (count of independent state-mutating surfaces), plus a rendered screenshot or captured pane output proving the new pane displays live data.
question_or_target: Extend the EXISTING monitor cockpit with a program pane reading EVENTS.jsonl and receipts read-only - explicitly NOT a new control plane, per spec line 10483. Exact question: after this unit, how many distinct control planes exist for program state, and is the answer one?
reviewer_requirement: independent-claude-reviewer plus an architecture reviewer on the duplicate-control-plane question
tests_required: read-only test asserting the pane cannot mutate program state; a census test asserting no second dispatcher was introduced.
title: Cockpit surface extending the existing monitor rather than a second control plane

evidence_requirement: Declared-versus-observed hook count with every missing marker named; a config-file listing is explicitly NOT accepted as evidence of loading.
question_or_target: Anchor spec:11303 (plugin appears installed but hooks are unloaded). Implement a POSITIVE load probe: each hook emits a load marker the verifier reads, so installed status is never inferred from the presence of a config file. Exact question: how many declared hooks actually emit their load marker at session start, and does that number equal the declared count?
reviewer_requirement: independent-claude-reviewer verifies the broken-state reading specifically
tests_required: both-states test: a deliberately malformed hook config must produce a LOWER observed count (proving the probe can see the broken state), and the repaired config must restore it. A probe silent in both states measures nothing.
title: Positive hook-load verification, not installed-status inference

evidence_requirement: Both-direction evidence: a revision argument surviving unconverted, AND a legitimate POSIX path argument still being converted correctly under the same configuration. A run showing only one direction is half a proof.
inputs: argument corpus (revisions, device paths, POSIX paths)
question_or_target: Anchor spec:11309 (PowerShell and Git Bash path rewriting). Implement path-conversion suppression that is COMMAND-aware and ARGUMENT-aware: applied around revision-shaped and device-path arguments, never globally, because a global suppression breaks legitimate POSIX path arguments and silently produces a no-op. Exact target: prove both failure directions are prevented, not just one.
reviewer_requirement: independent-claude-reviewer plus an adversarial refuter on the silent-no-op direction
tests_required: per-argument-shape test; a global-suppression fixture must FAIL the legitimate-path case, proving the scoped implementation is not equivalent to the global one.
title: Argument-aware shell path-rewriting control

evidence_requirement: Enumeration count over the fixture tree with and without the reserved-name file present; the counts must differ by exactly one and neither run may raise.
inputs: fixture tree containing reserved names and a >260 char path
question_or_target: Implement the path library that handles Windows extended-length paths and reserved device names (NUL, CON, AUX, PRN) without aborting a directory walk. Exact question: does a tree containing a file named NUL still enumerate completely, and what does the relative-path computation return for it?
tests_required: reserved-name test; long-path test above 260 characters; a control asserting the walk does NOT silently swallow the exception and return zero entries.
title: Path library for extended-length paths and reserved device names

evidence_requirement: Collision list with file, both keys, and the value each holds; a zero result must be accompanied by a planted-collision control proving the detector fires.
question_or_target: Anchor spec:11310 (case-insensitive parser collision on case-distinct JSON keys). Implement the detector that finds two keys differing only by case in any shipped config or manifest, before a case-insensitive consumer silently drops one. Exact question: how many such collisions exist across the shipped configuration surface today?
tests_required: planted-collision control; nested-object coverage test; a control asserting keys that differ by more than case are not reported.
title: Case-distinct key collision detector for configuration documents

evidence_requirement: Confusion matrix before and after on the historical corpus, with each surviving false positive shown as the raw record so the role-versus-text distinction is visible.
question_or_target: Anchor spec:11323 (false-positive prose and fixture detectors). Implement the shared library that classifies a match by its semantic ROLE - the tool-input verb, the JSON field, the AST position - rather than by the presence of a string in the payload, since a document describing a defect necessarily contains that defect's text. Exact question: on the historical false-positive corpus, what is the before-and-after false-positive rate?
reviewer_requirement: adversarial refuter constructs a mention that the library still fires on and a use it misses
tests_required: mention corpus (documents quoting a dangerous command) must produce zero fires; use corpus (actual invocation) must produce a fire on every entry. A library passing only one of the two corpora is not a fix.
title: Semantic-role detector library replacing payload-text matching
